subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these incident tickets.

judge.implied_focus: The nature/characterization of incidents (what is failing and how) derived from short_description text

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Classifies the incident into a substantive type, a core facet of characterizing what the incident is about.

per_column.name: incident_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Captures the manifested problem/symptom, a coherent facet of incident nature.

per_column.name: affected_asset_type
per_column.rationale: Identifies the asset involved, complementing category/symptom to describe the incident.

per_column.name: software_trigger
per_column.rationale: A causal attribute distinguishing software-driven vs other incidents; adds an analytically useful dimension.

per_column.name: self_resolved
per_column.rationale: A resolution-behavior attribute; slightly drifts toward outcome rather than incident nature but still ties to how incidents behave.

judge.rationale: The columns collectively centre on one inferable focus: characterizing the substance of each incident (category, symptom, affected asset) with two causal/behavioral attributes (software trigger, self-resolution). These are extracted from the free-text short_description rather than mechanical text metrics, and form a differentiated multi-facet structure at a useful granularity, not a single restatement. The focus is clearly actionable: an analyst can profile incident types, spot high-volume failure modes (e.g., printers not responding), and study self-resolution or software triggers. Minor drift: self_resolved leans toward outcome rather than incident nature, and category/asset_type overlap somewhat (both keyed on printer/monitor/etc.), slightly reducing structural crispness. Overall a coherent, actionable, well-structured focus proposal.
